title: Performance, emissions, and tribological assessment of spirulina‐based third‐generation biodiesel doped with metal oxide nanoparticles
content:
Abstract

Limited studies have examined the combined effects of various metal-oxide nanoparticles on engine performance, emissions, and tribological behavior when algae biodiesel is used as a fuel. This study investigates the effects of Al2O3, CeO2, and SiO2 nanoparticles dispersed in SAME20 (20% Spirulina algae methyl ester and 80% diesel) on diesel engine performance, emission, and tribological behavior. Three distinct nanoparticles at two concentrations (50 and 100 mg/L) were doped into the SAME20 blend, and their combustion, emissions, and wear characteristics were examined. The nanoparticle-doped fuels were prepared using magnetic stirring followed by ultrasonication to ensure stable dispersion. Experiments were conducted on a single-cylinder, four-stroke, water-cooled diesel engine under varying load conditions, while tribological behavior was assessed using a four-ball tribometer. Results indicated that nanoparticle addition significantly improved engine performance and reduced emissions compared to SAME20. The SAME20 + 100 mg/L Al2O3 blend achieved the highest BTE of 33.6% and the lowest BSFC of 0.214 kg/kWh at full load. Hydrocarbon, carbon monoxide, and smoke emissions were reduced by 19.49%, 26.47%, and 20.56%, respectively, while nitric oxide emissions increased slightly due to higher in-cylinder combustion temperatures. Tribological evaluation using a four-ball tribometer under standardized conditions (40 kg load, 1200 rpm, 75°C, 1 h) revealed substantial improvements, with SAME20 + 100 mg/L Al2O3 reducing the coefficient of friction and wear scar diameter by 36.02% and 35.3%, respectively, compared to SAME20, as confirmed by SEM analysis. Overall, SAME20 + 100 mg/L Al2O3 exhibited superior performance across all evaluated parameters.
